main_text.head: EXERC. VI.

head.i: eius caufis: de cœlo & eius uiribus.

main_text.p: QVoniam ad mistorum corporū procreationem quatuor prima rerum naturaliū elementa permisceri, mutarique oportet, idcirco de mistione nobis quoq; agendum est. Huius autem duplex statuitur genus: unum uidelicet, quod hominum opera fit: alterum naturæ solius.

Prioris generis duę sunt species, una ficco-rum, ueluti feminum tritici & hordei, quorum contactu tantum fit congeries, & non corpus unum: propterea quòd mistorum termini suas coĭeruant superficies. Etenim unumquodq; granum manet totum, neq; cum alio continuatur ad unum corpus effi-ciendum. Altera est liquidorum, cuiusmodi est oxicratum, crania [?] & mulsa. Tale corpus non est unum essentiali forma, sed tantum extremorum continuatione. Sic ex auro & argento commistis metallicum corpus ciniflones [?] fabricant. Veruntamē [?] à liquidis oleum excipimus, quod sua crassitudine cū aqua permisceri nequeat. Pofterius mistionis

page.notes: Handwritten word in the left margin, beside the first lines of the second paragraph, faint grey script ("Crama" or similar). Not printed, so not transcribed. Faint show-through text at upper right, not transcribed. "crania" is partly smudged by a stain, and the first letter is doubtful. "ciniflones" is doubtful. "Veruntamē" is doubtful (the vowel and abbreviation mark are hard to read). The catchword-like word "mistionis" at the foot of the text is the start of the printed word, continued on the next page.
